q: The Birkhoff ergodic theorem for a topological dynamical system implies that time averages along orbits converge for μ-almost every starting point. For a fully chaotic map like the doubling map Tx = 2x (mod 1):
opts: Time averages equal space averages for all x
Time averages equal space averages for Lebesgue-a.e. x (but not all x, since periodic points give rational averages)
Time averages equal the maximum of f
exp: Ergodicity of the doubling map w.r.t. Lebesgue measure: for a.e. x (in the Lebesgue sense), (1/n)Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} f(T^kx) → ∫f dx. Periodic points (countable set) give rational averages that typically differ from the space average.
